brief.greeting: Good morning. LLM agents tried to bottle their own tricks, but the bottles were half empty.

stories.headline: DeepMind releases lightweight multimodal embedder
stories.body: **Open, tiny, multimodal:** DeepMind unveiled EmbeddingGemma 2, a compact model that handles text and images without the usual GPU appetite. It’s ready for anyone who wants embeddings without a data center.
stories.why: You can add cross‑modal search to apps without blowing up memory or cost.

stories.headline: DySCo enables collaborative edge‑cloud LLM inference
stories.body: **Dynamic sharding, synced batches:** The DySCo paper introduces a system that splits LLM work between edge devices and the cloud, keeping token depth aligned. It reduces latency while preserving model quality.
stories.why: Your on‑device AI can stay fast without sacrificing the heavy lifting of the cloud.

stories.headline: DeepGEMM offers clean GPU matrix kernels
stories.body: **Efficient BLAS on GPUs:** DeepGEMM is a new library that provides tidy, high‑performance matrix‑multiply kernels for CUDA. It trims overhead compared to traditional BLAS stacks.
stories.why: Faster linear algebra means quicker training loops for your ML experiments.

quick_hits.text: **Benchmarks:** Agent‑in‑a‑Bottle shows 48 of 60 runs fall short of bottling expectations.
**Physics solvers:** WorldSolver tests LLMs on 168 simulation tasks from 61 classic graphics papers.
**Contract AI:** OpenAI and Ironclad train agents to handle complex contracting workflows.
**6G vision:** Split‑computing network aims to support holographic comms and drone anti‑collision.
**Security patches:** Tuesday updates hit AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora kernels and libraries.
**Atlassian tie‑up:** OpenAI expands to turn enterprise knowledge into actionable plans.

highlights.title: Agent in a Bottle: Can LLM Agents Turn Their Capabilities Into Cheap, Scalable Artifacts?
highlights.summary: The BOTTLED benchmark evaluates whether LLM agents can create cheaper, task‑specific solutions for large workloads, revealing that strong zero‑shot performance does not guarantee bottling ability.
highlights.detail: Agents receive an entire unlabeled workload and must stay within fixed time, compute, and API budgets, choosing approaches like training a small model or writing reusable code. Results show substantial variance among models with similar zero‑shot scores, highlighting a gap between general capability and cost‑effective specialization.

related.title: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution

highlights.title: WorldSolver: Can LLM Agents Simulate the Physical Dynamics via Solver Generation?
highlights.summary: WorldSolver benchmark tests LLM agents on generating physics solvers across 168 simulation tasks drawn from 61 classic graphics papers.
highlights.detail: Each task provides a code scaffold and fixed simulation environment, requiring agents to understand physics, formulate dynamics mathematically, and implement executable code. The benchmark spans domains such as fluid, cloth, and rigid body dynamics, offering a systematic way to assess agents' scientific reasoning and software engineering skills.

highlights.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: an open, lightweight multimodal embedding model
highlights.summary: EmbeddingGemma 2 is an open, lightweight multimodal embedding model released by DeepMind.
highlights.detail: The model is designed for efficient generation of embeddings from multiple modalities, targeting applications where resource constraints matter. Its open release enables the community to integrate multimodal representations without large compute overhead.

highlights.title: Evidence-Bound Reasoning: Neuro-Semantic Verification of Biomedical AI in Glioblastoma Radiogenomics
highlights.summary: A neuro‑semantic verification framework for glioblastoma radiogenomics aligns 1,728 MRI features with evidence records to enable deterministic claim checking.
highlights.detail: The system maps radiomic measurements from T1, T1GD, T2, and FLAIR sequences across three tumor regions into a shared semantic space, then evaluates transportability across cohorts and conducts a pilot LLM claim‑extraction. MGMT prediction was used as a stress test for model transport.

related.title: Comparison of techniques for fine-tuning open-weight models for entity extraction from radiology reports

highlights.title: Cleave: Scaling Tensor Program Optimization via Decoupled Algebraic Search and Operator Scheduling
highlights.summary: Cleave is an ML compiler that decouples algebraic graph transformations from operator scheduling using symbolic shapes.
highlights.detail: By performing superoptimization on shape‑symbolic graphs, Cleave quickly checks equivalence and introduces a Split operator with a symbolic count, enabling efficient fusion of reduction‑heavy kernels such as FlashAttention. The approach separates search spaces, making large‑scale kernel generation more tractable.

items.title: Advancing computer use with Ironclad
items.summary: OpenAI and Ironclad are training AI agents to handle complex contracting workflows, aiming to advance computer use for professional work.
items.detail: The collaboration focuses on evaluating agents that can interpret, draft, and negotiate contracts, integrating legal domain knowledge with general AI capabilities. Success could reduce manual effort in legal document processing and set precedents for AI‑assisted professional tasks.

items.title: Atlassian and OpenAI expand partnership to turn enterprise knowledge into action
items.summary: Atlassian and OpenAI are expanding their partnership to connect frontier models with enterprise knowledge, helping teams plan, build, and deliver work.
items.detail: The extended integration will allow Atlassian's suite to leverage large language models for knowledge retrieval, task automation, and decision support, aiming to streamline collaborative workflows across enterprises.

items.title: Security updates for Tuesday
items.summary: LWN reports Tuesday security updates for multiple Linux distributions, including AlmaLinux, Debian, and Fedora, covering a wide range of packages such as the kernel, libpcap, and Ruby.
items.detail: The updates address vulnerabilities across core system components and popular applications, with each distro publishing its own package list. AlmaLinux updates include the real‑time kernel, while Debian patches libraries like libpng and LibreOffice. Fedora’s rollout spans from the Chromium browser to the OCaml toolchain, reflecting a coordinated effort to harden the ecosystem.

items.title: SmallTV Hacking With Surprisingly Little Fuss
items.summary: GeekMagic SmallTV devices can be hacked with minimal effort to add custom firmware and functionality.
items.detail: These low‑cost microcontroller‑display combos are popular for hobby projects; the hack involves opening the case, flashing new code, and repurposing the screen for user‑defined output. The process requires only basic soldering and a serial connection.

items.title: OpenSSH 10.6 released
items.summary: OpenSSH 10.6 adds a hybrid post‑quantum ssh‑mldsa44‑ed25519 signature algorithm and disables the LZ77 compression coder.
items.detail: The release also introduces a new -p flag for sftp lmkdir/mkdir commands and re‑enables more frequent patch cycles due to a surge in AI‑assisted bug reports. The compression change reduces side‑channel leakage at the cost of lower compression efficiency.

items.title: [$] Last rites for Gentoo's Chromium package
items.summary: Gentoo maintainers have abandoned the Chromium package due to its complex build system and frequent upstream releases.
items.detail: Chromium’s bundled dependencies and rapid version turnover made automated packaging impractical, leading to repeated breakages and user complaints. The decision reflects broader challenges in maintaining large, fast‑moving upstream projects within source‑based distributions.

items.title: [$] Python's two modules for random numbers
items.summary: Python added the secrets module in version 3.6 (2016) to provide cryptographically secure random numbers for passwords and tokens.
items.detail: The older random module remains unsuitable for security‑critical uses, and despite documentation warnings it is still occasionally misused. The secrets API offers functions like token_bytes and token_urlsafe that draw from the operating system’s CSPRNG.

items.title: DySCo: Dynamic Sharding for Collaborative Edge-Cloud LLM Inference with Depth-Synchronized Batching
items.summary: DySCo introduces dynamic sharding and depth‑synchronized batching to run LLM inference collaboratively across edge devices and the cloud.
items.detail: The system keeps KV caches local on the edge and uses a dyForward executor to run contiguous layer ranges without reloading weights, reducing idle gaps and allowing heterogeneous requests to be batched efficiently. This improves latency for IoT applications that rely on large language models.

items.title: 6G NeXt - Towards 6G Split Computing Network Applications: Use Cases and Architecture
items.summary: The 6G NeXt project proposes a split‑computing network architecture to support holographic communications and drone anti‑collision systems, requiring high‑speed distributed backbone computing and tight integration with wireless networks.
items.detail: Both use cases involve widely distributed clients that must cooperate, with holographic communication demanding substantial processing power. The architecture relies on a distributed backbone to meet heterogeneous latency and bandwidth requirements, aiming to deliver consistent quality of service across the network.

items.title: cathrynlavery/diagram-design
items.summary: The diagram-design repository offers 42 editorial diagram types for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Factory Droid, and Pi, delivered as self‑contained HTML and SVG without shadows or Mermaid.
items.detail: Each diagram is packaged in a single HTML file embedding SVG graphics, making it easy to integrate into documentation or presentations. The collection avoids external dependencies, ensuring consistent rendering across browsers. It targets developers needing clear visualizations of AI tool architectures.

items.title: dortania/OpenCore-Legacy-Patcher
items.summary: OpenCore-Legacy-Patcher is a Python utility that modifies OpenCore to restore the pre‑patch macOS experience on legacy hardware.
items.detail: The tool automates patching of bootloader components, allowing older Macs to run newer macOS versions with minimal configuration. It focuses on compatibility rather than performance enhancements, and it is maintained by the Dortania community.

items.title: falcosecurity/falco
items.summary: Falco is an open‑source cloud‑native runtime security engine that monitors system calls to detect suspicious activity.
items.detail: Developed by the Falco Security team, it integrates with Kubernetes and other orchestration platforms, emitting alerts based on customizable rule sets. It runs as a daemon on hosts, providing real‑time threat detection without requiring agents on containers.

items.title: ggml-org/llama.cpp
items.summary: llama.cpp implements large language model inference in pure C/C++, enabling CPU‑only execution without external libraries.
items.detail: The project focuses on minimal dependencies and portability, allowing users to run models on modest hardware. It supports quantization techniques to reduce memory usage and includes example scripts for common model formats.
